sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

This petition under Section 24 of CPC is filed by the petitioner-wife seeking for transfer of M.C.No.296/2022 pending on the file of the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkur to the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Srinivasapura.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of the respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 20.10.2019 at Nandini Palace, Kalahasthipura, Near D.C.Office, NH-75, Kolar as per Hindu rites and customs.
After the marriage, the petitioner was residing with her husband at her matrimonial house at Tumkur.
As matrimonial disputes arose between the parties, the petitioner started living separately with her parents in Srinivasapura.

Thereafter, the respondent-husband filed a NC:
2024:KHC:19261 divorce petition under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in M.C.No.296/2022 before the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that since the petitioner is residing in Srinivasapura, it would cause inconvenience and great hardship for her to travel a distance of 140 kms to Tumkur to prosecute the case.
Hence, she filed the present petition seeking for transfer of case.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner-wife contended that after the marriage, the petitioner was residing at her matrimonial house.
Thereafter, due to matrimonial disputes, the petitioner started living separately with her parents in Srinivasapura Taluk.

He further contended that the respondent-husband filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in M.C.No.296/2022 before the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The parents of the petitioner are aged persons and she has no other relatives or family NC: 2024:KHC:19261 members to assist her in traveling to Tumkur, which is at a distance of 140 kms to prosecute the case.
Therefore, if the petition is not transferred, it would cause great inconvenience and hardship to the petitioner-wife.

He further contended that the petitioner-wife has filed petition in Crl.Misc.No.143/2022 before the Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Srinivaspura and the respondent- husband is appearing through his counsel in the said case.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Srinivaspura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The wife also filed criminal case in C.C.No.245/2022 under Section 498A of IPC.
He further contended that in the divorce petition, the parties are said to be agreed to settle the matter but so far the respondent has not come forward.
Hence, he sought for allowing the petition.
4. The respondent is served and unrepresented.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Perused the petition papers.

It is not in dispute that the petitioner is the legally wedded wife of the respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 20.10.2019 at Nandini Palace, Kalahasthipura, Near D.C.Office, NH-75,
Kolar as per Hindu rites and customs.
After the marriage, the petitioner was residing with her husband at her matrimonial house at Tumkur.

As matrimonial disputes arose between the parties,
the petitioner started living separately with her parents in Srinivasapura.
Thereafter, the respondent- husband filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in M.C.No.296/2022 before the I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Tumkuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case of the petitioner is that since the petitioner is residing in Srinivasapura, it would cause inconvenience and great hardship for her to travel a distance of 140 kms to Tumkur to prosecute the case.

This Court in the case Smt.M.V.Rekha v. Sri Sathya @ Suraj - ILR 2010 KAR 5407 at Paragraph No.15 has held as hereunder:
"The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that ends of justice demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.

entities.text: Smt.M.V.Rekha v. Sri Sathya @ Suraj - ILR 2010 KAR 5407
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of either of the parties, the social strata of the spouses and behavioural pattern, their standard of life antecedent to marriage and subsequent thereon and the circumstances of either of the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
Generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.

Further, when two proceedings in different Courts which raise common question of fact and law and when the decisions are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to NC: 2024:KHC:19261 avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions (See Smt.NandaKishori v. S.B.Shiua Prakash AIR 1993 Kar 87, Sumita Singh v. Kumar Sanjay and Anr.
MANU/SC/0936/2001:AIR 2002 SC 396 and Smt.Swarna Gouri v. Sri Vinayak Pujar MANU/KA/7130/2007 : ILR 2007 Kar 4561."
(emphasis supplied)
8.

entities.text: Smt.NandaKishori v. S.B.Shiua Prakash AIR 1993 Kar 87
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sumita Singh v. Kumar Sanjay and Anr.
MANU/SC/0936/2001:AIR 2002 SC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Smt.Swarna Gouri v. Sri Vinayak Pujar MANU/KA/7130/2007 : ILR 2007 Kar 4561
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, taking note of the inconvenience as made out by the petitioner and the law laid down in the case of Smt.M.V.Rekha (supra), which provides that convenience of the wife is an aspect that is to be taken note of while considering the transfer petitions, petition deserves to be allowed.

9. Accordingly, the following order is passed:
Smt K P Bhanushaa vs Sri J Pradeep on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116300614/
3 ORDER a) The petition is allowed.
b) The case in M.C.No.296/2022 on the file of the I Additional Principal Judge,
Family Court, Tumkur is NC: 2024:KHC:19261 hereby withdrawn and the same is transferred to the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Srinivasapura.
c) The transferor Court is hereby directed to transmit the entire records to the transferee court.
d) The transferee Court after hearing the parties is directed to dispose of the said case as expeditiously as possible and in accordance with law.
